local-profile code runner under Lambda-first: docker compose local dev needs either the headspace runner, a Lambda-compatible local emulator, or accepting cloud-only code nodes during development — undecided
Phase-1 observability floor is undecided: which metrics, probes, and log surfaces ship in the first slice (full OTel is Phase 2) — probes are covered by c23, the rest is plan detail

Cost containment before Phase 4: per-run cost/token budget enforcement is PRD Phase 4, so until then engine loop/visit/time bounds are the only containment for Lambda and agent spend — accepted as residual risk for early phases

scope_entries.finding: the core stack is already decided, not open for redesign: Go control plane, React/Vite/React Flow UI, Postgres authoritative, SQS as signal only, JSON Schema 2020-12, CEL, content-addressed versions — the app design implements the PRD

the engine is provider-neutral with an HTTP/JSON actor protocol (sync 200 / async 202 + callbacks, idempotency keys); claude-agent-sdk, claude-agent-api, and colleague all attach as external adapters, never engine branches
code executes only through the headspace-cli runner adapter as a separate deployment; no Docker socket, no in-process scripts in any control-plane container

the ledger authority model (proposed/confirmed/observed/derived, execution vs assurance) is a runtime rule every surface must enforce, and its dashed-vs-solid rendering maps onto the org site's edge convention

leases, fencing tokens, SKIP LOCKED claims, transactional outbox, and the recovery matrix are exactly the multi-pod-safety machinery the user requires; deployment ordering reweights to k8s-first per user instruction, recorded as a PRD deviation

progressive detail, read-only Run+Ledger first slice, keyboard + reduced-motion are PRD requirements matching the user's clean-design/no-prose ask; the design source must be extracted and revision-pinned, never copied by eye
Milestones 0/1 and the acceptance checklist already define the buildable slice — contracts+compiler, then the durable vertical slice with the changes_required loop and headspace evidence

subprocess is the only integration — no daemon, HTTP, or queue; frozen additive 0-8 exit band and nine-section result package; PRD §13.7's operation contract exceeds the shipped surface (profiles not per-op images, no snapshot flags, no schema artifact), so the Go adapter bridges and declares gaps honestly

plan waves --json is a ready-made design-time import (wave layering + per-task instruction/acceptance/covers); the CLI stays deterministic and non-orchestrating, so Culture Nodes consumes exports and never pushes runtime state back except deviate/summary; its error/output/exit conventions are the family standard to mirror

drift-tested contract v1: work --json/--background subprocess dispatch, flight feed/control files for monitor+steer, three-way ok/error/incomplete exit mapping, no socket ever — the actor adapter must be a bridge process, and AGENTS.colleague.md + --role/--mode is the whole per-node behavior seam

ec2bedrock-cli makes zero AWS calls by design — the real models are ec2-cli (single client factory, lazy boto3, name-based error mapping, aws_call env-error split, review-then-apply teardown) and open-bedrock-server's credential chain (role ARN, IRSA, profile, keys, ambient); bedrock-budgeteer shows naming/tagging but uses SQS only as DLQs, so SQS-as-work-signal has no local precedent

Astro 7 static site; the entire design system is one framework-agnostic custom-property file plus fontsource fonts — no shared package exists, so extraction from a pinned org revision is the path; terminal 7-color palette fits node kinds; dashed=proposed/solid=confirmed edge semantics are load-bearing sitewide; Apache-2.0 code grant, trademark not covered

webglass is a guarded evidence plane, not a test framework: apps become testable by publishing an agent-state JSON node, stable ids/data-attrs, keyboard operability, and a declared-targets policy profile; no click/drag exists, so canvas gestures need Playwright directly

today's package is the zero-dependency teken-gated mesh-agent scaffold with a colleague-backend identity; product work must not break it, and where the Go monorepo lands relative to it is a pending user decision

multi-pod parallel safety and docker/k8s-native packaging are confirmed requirements; agent runtimes are trigger-only externals — another system holds colleague / claude-agent-sdk / claude-agent-api and culture-nodes invokes them remotely, so actor adapters are part of the hosting system, not the culture-nodes deployment

code run uses AWS Lambda for now — resolves the k8s runner-topology blocker for the first slice (no Docker engine needed in the k8s profile) and defers the headspace Docker adapter to local/later; Lambda runner limits (15-minute cap, stateless workspace via S3) become contract constraints to declare

the product is Go-only end to end — CLI included — with Python-family CLI logic cited/copied into Go; deployment is minimal (one Go binary + Postgres) with all code execution external (Lambda now, a local headspace-cli bridge for dev); this resolves q1 and simplifies q2

python is a thin CLI front and react-flow a thin web front over one Go-owned API; Postgres is the only db unless proven unfit (embeddings may justify a second store later); SQS confirmed as the AWS queue signal
agent backends including codex run on different machines/containers external to culture-nodes — the actor boundary is a network boundary, not a co-located process boundary

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / hooks (user finding): agent-node lifecycle
scope_entries.finding: the user surfaced a missing dimension — engine-controlled pre/post-run code around external agent steps; landed as a first-class requirement with failure semantics (pre-run failure blocks dispatch; post-run failure is a domain outcome, never silent)

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / hidden-dependency lens: resolved q4 x prd-spec §23 phasing
scope_entries.finding: moving multi-pod safety to Phase 1 silently invalidated Phase-2 artifact phasing — filesystem artifacts break at replicas>1; artifact storage must be pod-agnostic from Phase 1

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / migration lens: c23 rolling updates x Postgres schema
scope_entries.finding: k8s-first rolling updates need an explicit migration policy: expand-contract, migrate-before-rollout, N-1 binary compatibility — absent from the spec until now

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / failure-mode lens: AWS Lambda hard quotas x c25
scope_entries.finding: Lambda's 15-minute and 6MB limits must be compile-time validation rules, not runtime surprises; the PRD's own example test node timeout (15m) sits exactly at the cap

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / security lens: Lambda IAM + callback ingress
scope_entries.finding: two privilege boundaries were unstated: the worker must only invoke registry-pinned functions (no wildcard IAM), and external agents need a reachable, token-guarded callback ingress in the k8s profile

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / adjacent-systems lens: publish.yml x helm image supply
scope_entries.finding: the repo's only release lane today is PyPI; helm and compose need published multi-arch container images by digest — a container release lane is a real missing deliverable

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / overlooked-actors lens: Phase-1 actor registration
scope_entries.finding: actors exist from Phase 1 but auth is phased to Phase 2; static config-declared registration is the honest interim assumption, and the Phase-1 auth posture needs a user decision (q5)

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / concurrency lens: c22 machinery
scope_entries.finding: clean pass — leases, fencing, SKIP LOCKED, outbox, and the two-worker fault tests already cover the claiming path; residual concurrency risk lives in the recorded parks, none new found

not read this pass: the culture mesh repos (culture, agentirc, culture-core) whose identity/trust model may later inform actor registration, and the claude-agent-sdk / claude-agent-api concrete surfaces (already parked v3) — findings there would land in a future pass, and no claim in this spec cites them
